name: Flow-preserving Euler rule (E_ZX)
summary: A Hadamard edge between spiders with phases α₁ and α₂ can be replaced by a path through three new spiders with phases β₁, β₂, β₃, moving the phases α₁, α₂ onto the path.
description:
This is the [Euler-angle rule with a Hadamard](../euler-angles-hadamard/) in graph-like form. Unfusing the phases of the two spiders, the left-hand side contains $R_Z(\alpha_2)HR_Z(\alpha_1)$ on the edge, and the path on the right-hand side is $HR_Z(\beta_3)HR_Z(\beta_2)HR_Z(\beta_1)H = R_X(\beta_3)R_Z(\beta_2)R_X(\beta_1)$, so the two sides are equal up to the global phase $e^{i\gamma}$ by Vilmart's formulas.

Backens and Perdrix use this form in their complete set of flow-preserving rewrite rules. In MBQC terms the two spiders are XY-measured vertices $a$ and $b$ (with angles $\alpha_1$ and $\alpha_2$) and the rule inserts three new XY-measured vertices $x, y, z$ on the edge between them, while $a$ and $b$ get angle 0. It preserves extended causal flow when the flow corrects $a$ by $b$ (or $b$ by $a$): the new flow is $a\mapsto x\mapsto y\mapsto z\mapsto b$. It is only needed in this causal-flow setting, where it is used to translate the Euler rule of the complete equational theory for quantum circuits.

The stored instance is checked for $\alpha_1=\frac\pi3$, $\alpha_2=\frac{2\pi}7$.
parameter_notes: The two spiders have n and m further legs (shown for n = m = 2); they may have any number of further legs and Hadamard edges.
conditions: β₁, β₂, β₃ (in [0, 2π)) and γ are functions of α₁, α₂: let z = −sin((α₁+α₂)/2) + i cos((α₁−α₂)/2) and z′ = cos((α₁+α₂)/2) − i sin((α₁−α₂)/2). If z′ = 0 then β₁ = 2 arg z, β₂ = β₃ = 0; if z = 0 then β₁ = 2 arg z′, β₂ = π, β₃ = 0; otherwise β₁ = arg z + arg z′, β₂ = 2 arg(i + |z/z′|) and β₃ = arg z − arg z′. The global phase is γ = (α₁+α₂)/2 − arg z + (π − β₂)/2 (with arg 0 = 0), except when z = 0, where γ = (α₁+α₂)/2 − arg z′. Flow: the rule preserves extended causal flow if the diagram has an extended causal flow g with g(a) = {b} or g(b) = {a}, where a and b are the two XY-measured vertices.
notes: The build checks one generic instance of the angles; `python authoring/flow_preserving.py --selftest` checks the formulas with PyZX on random angles and on the two degenerate cases.
